solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Loading area number two reported new delivery (4)

indicatorNotes.reported: what is reported is heard, so we go by the sound of the words

blocks.note: a loading bay
B is second in the alphabet, as in plan B
said aloud, bay-bee

annotation.surface: A warehouse announcement that a second consignment has arrived at the dock.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all goods-in logistics; the delivery the definition means is a birth.
annotation.definitionFit: A baby is what a mother delivers, so a new delivery.

entries.clue: Cheap lager? Add to basket (6)

blocks.note: an adjective for low-priced goods, as airlines and hotels are sold
Bud, short for Budweiser, a brand of lager
to get something is to add it to your shopping

annotation.surface: An online shopper popping a bargain beer into their basket.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the brand name: BUD is Budweiser, and adding it to the basket means you GET it.
annotation.definitionFit: Budget as an adjective means low-priced, cheap.

entries.clue: Republican in group eats at a funny time (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the letter for Republican goes in the word for group

blocks.note: a bunch is a group
R = Republican, placed inside the group word after its first letter

annotation.surface: A party member in some clique grabs a meal at an odd hour.
annotation.walkthrough: "Eats" reads as a verb, but here it is the slang noun for food: brunch is eats taken at a funny time, between breakfast and lunch.
annotation.definitionFit: Brunch is a meal eaten at an in-between hour, neither breakfast nor lunch.

entries.clue: Cold, tender spot in heel checked for sensitivity (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the tender spot goes inside the word for heel

blocks.note: C = cold, on taps
the heel of a loaf is its end
a sore is a tender spot, placed in END: EN(SORE)D

annotation.surface: A chilly, blistered heel being examined for how much it hurts.
annotation.walkthrough: "Sensitivity" and "tender" pull toward a sore foot; the definition means material vetted for anything that could offend.
annotation.definitionFit: Censored material has been checked and cut for anything sensitive.

entries.clue: Nearly all large parts shortened about 20 inches (5)

indicatorNotes.Nearly all: keep all but the last letter
indicatorNotes.parts: BI parts the word for shortened, sitting between its letters

blocks.note: cut = shortened
BIG without its last letter, set between CU and T

annotation.surface: Most big pieces have been trimmed down to around twenty inches.
annotation.walkthrough: "Parts" looks like a noun belonging to "large"; it is the verb, BI parting CUT.
annotation.definitionFit: The cubit was an ancient measure, forearm length, of roughly 18 to 21 inches.

entries.clue: Whinge at drunken Romeo’s snoring habit? (9)

indicatorNotes.drunken: the letters stagger about into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone complaining about a drunk called Romeo who keeps snoring.
annotation.walkthrough: A habit here is clothing, as a monk's habit is: what you wear to bed and snore in. The question mark marks that stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: Nightwear is the clothing, the habit, worn while sleeping and snoring.

entries.clue: English company incorporated by professed animal killer traded freely (4-3- 7)

indicatorNotes.incorporated by: the English company is taken inside the professed animal killer

blocks.note: openly declared
a hunter kills animals; E and CO go in after its H
E = English
CO = company

annotation.surface: A British firm taken over by an avowed hunter, its shares then freely dealt.
annotation.walkthrough: The professed animal killer is broken open after its first letter so the English company can sit inside. Over-the-counter trading happens directly between parties, outside a formal exchange.
annotation.definitionFit: Over-the-counter securities are traded directly between parties, freely, off the exchange.

entries.clue: Paint large bird and small that cat’s caught (8)

indicatorNotes.caught: the cat has caught the S, so it sits inside LION

blocks.note: the emu is a large flightless bird
a lion is a big cat
S = small, caught inside LION: L(S)ION

annotation.surface: An instruction to paint a big bird and the little one the cat got.
annotation.walkthrough: "Paint" reads as an order to an artist; it is the noun, emulsion being the everyday wall paint.
annotation.definitionFit: Emulsion is water-based paint used on walls and ceilings.

entries.clue: Criminal here stood for sharing wealth, primarily (8,6)

annotation.definition: Criminal here stood for sharing wealth, primarily

indicatorNotes.Criminal: the letters are made crooked, rearranged
indicatorNotes.primarily: take the first letters of sharing and wealth

blocks.note: anagram fodder
first letters of sharing and wealth
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A historical note on where a famous outlaw lived who stood for redistributing wealth.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Robin Hood, the outlaw who robbed the rich to give to the poor, made his home in Sherwood Forest.
annotation.definitionFit: Sherwood Forest in Nottinghamshire is legendary home of Robin Hood, the criminal who shared out wealth.

entries.clue: Awful blister that hurt in bed after Georgia rolled over (6,3)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' means placed inside, so OUCH goes into the reversed letters
indicatorNotes.after: 'after' means following, so BED is written after GA
indicatorNotes.rolled over: GABED is turned round to DEBAG

blocks.note: GA is the US state abbreviation
after GA: GABED, then turned round to DEBAG
what you say when something hurts, set in after the first letter

annotation.surface: A painful blister makes a night in a Georgia bed miserable.
annotation.walkthrough: "Blister" suggests a skin complaint; in slang it is an irritating person, so the definition is an insult.
annotation.definitionFit: Douchebag is slang for a contemptible person, an awful blister.

entries.clue: Supply crack online? (5)

blocks.note: E = electronic, as in e-mail
a crack is a witty remark

annotation.surface: Asking where to get hold of drugs on the internet.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points at drugs; crack here is a wisecrack.
annotation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to supply them with what they need.

entries.clue: Operation involving subs going north not what it seems (6)

indicatorNotes.involving: to involve is to include, so OP takes DUES inside it
indicatorNotes.going north: in a down answer, going north turns the letters upward, reversing them

blocks.note: OP = operation
subs = subscriptions, dues; placed inside OP before the whole is reversed

annotation.surface: A naval operation with submarines heading north that is not what it seems.
annotation.walkthrough: "Subs" suggests submarines; it is short for subscriptions, dues paid to a club.
annotation.definitionFit: Pseudo means sham, not what it appears to be.

entries.clue: Bit of work first for recycler, leaving out bottles (7)

indicatorNotes.first: take the first letter of recycler
indicatorNotes.bottles: the phrase for leaving out holds R inside it

blocks.note: except = leaving out
first letter of recycler, held inside the phrase for leaving out

annotation.surface: A recycler's first job is to sort out the glass bottles.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bottles" looks like the recycling; it is a verb, holding the R in.
annotation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a passage taken from a longer work.

entries.clue: Where “Sans teeth, sans eyes, sans…” leads? (As You Like It) (2,5)

annotation.definition2: Where “Sans teeth, sans eyes, sans…” leads

blocks.clueFragment: Where “Sans teeth, sans eyes, sans…” leads
blocks.note: Jaques's seven ages speech: the next item in the list after eyes
a recipe phrase meaning in whatever amount you prefer

annotation.surface: A quotation from Jaques's speech on the seven ages of man, with its play named.
annotation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a source reference; it is the second definition. The line in As You Like It runs "Sans teeth, sans eyes, sans taste, sans everything".
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: the next word of Jaques's line is the flavour sense, and a cook seasoning by that sense adds as much as you like.

entries.clue: Perhaps keep string to wrap present officially (3,3,6)

indicatorNotes.Perhaps: a fort is one example of a keep
indicatorNotes.to wrap: the keep and the string together wrap round HERE

blocks.note: a keep is a castle stronghold, a fort for example
present = here, as in a register
cord is string

annotation.surface: Advice to hang on to the string from a gift you are wrapping.
annotation.walkthrough: "Present" reads as a gift to wrap; it means here, as in answering a register, and the keep and the string wrap it from either side.
annotation.definitionFit: Saying something for the record puts it on the official record.

entries.clue: Sinner top sort of this? (6,3)

indicatorNotes.sort of: sort as a verb: sort the letters into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A wrongdoer at the top of a class of wrongdoers.
annotation.walkthrough: Jannik Sinner is the Italian world number one tennis player, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: Jannik Sinner is the world's leading tennis professional, so the whole clue reads straight as a description of the answer.

entries.clue: Funny sitrep entertaining intelligence (6)

indicatorNotes.Funny: the letters are in a funny, odd order

blocks.note: anagram fodder; a sitrep is a military situation report
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: An amusing situation report full of military intelligence.
annotation.walkthrough: "Intelligence" reads as military information to go with sitrep; the definition means lively wit.
annotation.definitionFit: Esprit is lively, amusing wit: entertaining intelligence.

entries.clue: Lover bound architect’s splayed ribs (3,5)

blocks.note: a lover of something is a fan
to bound or leap is to vault

annotation.surface: A lover leaping over an architect's splayed ribs, as if in a strange accident.
annotation.walkthrough: "Ribs" suggests a body; these are an architect's stone ribs spreading out like a fan across a ceiling.
annotation.definitionFit: A fan vault is a ceiling whose ribs spread out from each column like an opened fan.

entries.clue: Space on packed bus replacement service for jilted bride? (8,4)

blocks.note: where you stand when the seats are full
split the answer after STAND: a stand-in for the absent groom

annotation.surface: A rail replacement bus so crammed it seems to be full of wedding guests.
annotation.walkthrough: "Replacement service" reads as the bus that stands in for a train; read STANDING ROOM as STAND-IN GROOM and the jilted bride has her substitute.
annotation.definitionFit: Standing room is the space left for standing passengers when a bus is full.

entries.clue: Index for one name (6)

blocks.note: the index is the pointing digit, one example of the class
to identify someone to the police as the culprit

annotation.surface: A note that an index is one kind of list of names.
annotation.walkthrough: "Index" suggests the back of a book; here it is the pointing finger. To finger a suspect is to name them.
annotation.definitionFit: Finger as a verb means to identify or name someone, usually as guilty.

entries.clue: Characters edging over East River in New York habitually cross there (6)

indicatorNotes.Characters edging: take the letters on the edges of over
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' means placed inside, so E and R sit within NY

blocks.note: the outer letters of over
NY = New York
E = East, inside NY
R = River, inside NY after E: N(ER)Y

annotation.surface: New Yorkers crossing the East River, as they do every day.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cross" looks like crossing the river; it means bad-tempered. "There" signals the word is American, ornery being US dialect.
annotation.definitionFit: Ornery is American for cantankerous, habitually bad-tempered.

entries.clue: Artist and half orchestral players stuffed envelopes (7)

indicatorNotes.half: keep half the letters of violinists

blocks.note: RA = Royal Academician
the first half of VIOLINISTS

annotation.surface: A painter and some orchestra members sit stuffing envelopes for a mailing.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stuffed envelopes" reads as office work; ravioli are little pasta envelopes stuffed with filling.
annotation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small pasta parcels, envelopes of dough with a stuffing.

entries.clue: On the way back, strap down load on bike (7)

blocks.note: a rein is a strap
the nap on cloth is its soft down; REINNAP is then read backwards

annotation.surface: A cyclist on the return trip straps their luggage onto the bike.
annotation.walkthrough: "Down" looks like a direction for strapping; it means the soft fluff or nap of a fabric.
annotation.definitionFit: A pannier is a bag carried on a bicycle rack, a load on a bike.

entries.clue: Place just a train ride from London remains sub-standard (5)

annotation.definition: Place just a train ride from London

indicatorNotes.sub-: sub means under: in a down answer, IS goes below PAR

blocks.note: in golf the standard score for a hole
to remain is to be, placed under PAR

annotation.surface: A complaint that some place near London stays below standard.
annotation.walkthrough: "Sub-standard" reads as one word meaning poor; split it, sub is the instruction to put IS under PAR. Paris is a Eurostar ride from London.
annotation.definitionFit: Paris is reached from London by the Eurostar train through the Channel Tunnel.

entries.clue: Conservative blocks loyal campaigners’ suspension (5)

indicatorNotes.blocks: C sits inside TRUE, blocking its middle

blocks.note: true = loyal
C = Conservative, set inside the word for loyal

annotation.surface: A Tory politician gets faithful party campaigners suspended.
annotation.walkthrough: "Suspension" suggests a disciplinary ban; it is a suspension of fighting between warring campaigners.
annotation.definitionFit: A truce is a suspension of hostilities between those campaigning against each other.

entries.clue: Darwin’s ship led by sound of miserable shark (9)

indicatorNotes.sound of: we want a spelling that sounds like the word for miserable
indicatorNotes.led by: POR comes first, in front of BEAGLE

blocks.note: poor = miserable
HMS Beagle carried Darwin round the world

annotation.surface: An account of Darwin's voyage being shadowed by a sorrowful-sounding shark.
annotation.walkthrough: The porbeagle is a North Atlantic shark; its first syllable is pronounced like poor.
annotation.definitionFit: The porbeagle is a mackerel shark of the North Atlantic.

entries.clue: Irish drunk promises to pay after second dram (8)

indicatorNotes.after: IOUS comes after S and TOT

blocks.note: S = second
a dram or tot is a small measure of spirits
IOUs are written promises to pay

annotation.surface: A drunk Irishman offers to settle up after another whiskey.
annotation.walkthrough: Stotious is Irish slang for very drunk, and "Irish drunk" is an adjective meaning that, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: the word is Irish (and Scots) slang for very drunk, so the definition names both the sense and where it is spoken.

entries.clue: Host taking book from off his trolley (4)

indicatorNotes.taking: take away the letter for book
indicatorNotes.from: the book is taken from the word for off his trolley

blocks.note: barmy = crazy; off one's trolley is British slang for mad
B = book, removed from the front of BARMY

annotation.surface: A party host who has lost his mind.
annotation.walkthrough: "Host" reads as a party giver; its older sense is a great number of soldiers, an army.
annotation.definitionFit: An old sense of host is a great body of soldiers, as in the heavenly host or Lord of Hosts.
